name: communication-style-profile
description: Captures the specialist's voice and formatting defaults as durable rules: style rules destined for Custom Instructions, and discrete facts destined for Copilot Memory.
when_to_use: Once, when first setting up Copilot personalization, and again whenever the specialist's writing style or stated preferences change materially.
what_to_use_for: Turning writing samples, stated preferences, and role context into two clearly separated outputs: durable style rules for Custom Instructions, and discrete facts for Copilot Memory.
required_inputs: Writing samples (a few representative emails or documents); Stated preferences (anything the specialist explicitly wants followed, e.g. "no em dashes"); Role (the specialist's role and context)
expected_outputs: Style rules for Custom Instructions (voice, formatting defaults, do/don't list, phrase bank); Discrete facts for Copilot Memory, each phrased as a "Remember that ..." statement; Install footer naming the owning Copilot layer and load steps
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: capture the specialist's communication style as two separated durable outputs, one for Custom Instructions and one for Copilot Memory.

You should have these inputs: (1) writing samples, (2) stated preferences, (3) the specialist's role. If any input is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Privacy rule: business role information only; no personal phone numbers or home emails, no performance or personality judgments about colleagues, and prefer role labels over named individuals where the role suffices.

Method:
1. Read the writing samples, stated preferences, and role provided below.
2. Derive style rules: voice (formal/informal, first/third person, sentence length tendencies), formatting defaults (bullet vs prose, heading use, no em dashes if that is a stated preference), a do/don't list, and a short phrase bank of wording the specialist tends to reuse. Write these as rules for Custom Instructions.
3. Separately, derive discrete facts worth remembering (role, team, recurring correspondents by role, standing preferences not about style) as short factual statements for Copilot Memory, each phrased so it can be pasted into chat as "Remember that <fact>".
4. Do not invent a preference not evidenced in the writing samples or explicitly stated; if a stylistic pattern is only weakly evidenced, note it as tentative rather than asserting it as a firm rule.
5. End with an install footer: style rules go into Custom Instructions (Copilot Chat, Settings and more, Chat settings, Personalization); Memory facts are seeded by telling Copilot "Remember that <fact>" in chat, one fact per message, then verified and pruned in the same Personalization pane (the pane itself is view and delete only; verify against your own tenant, since menus and rollout vary). Note that behavioral-rule propagation into inline Word/Excel/Outlook authoring is partial and rolling, so the specialist should verify the rules actually apply in each surface they use. Include a one-line verification step: ask Copilot a style-revealing question and confirm the response reflects the installed rules.

Source of truth: the writing samples, stated preferences, and role provided below are the only sources.

This is durable context for the specialist to review and install themselves; it never installs itself, and it never asserts a preference the samples do not support.

Do not fabricate a preference, a fact, or a phrase not evidenced in the inputs.

name: stakeholder-and-contact-map
description: Maps who the specialist interacts with and how each connects to them, as durable context for Copilot Memory or a private declarative agent's knowledge.
when_to_use: Once, when first setting up durable context, and again whenever stakeholders or interaction patterns change materially.
what_to_use_for: Turning a contact list, roles, and interaction cadence into a structured contact map with an install footer.
expected_outputs: Contact map (who, role, connection to the specialist, cadence, channel); Install footer naming the owning Copilot layer and load steps
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: build a stakeholder and contact map from a contact list, roles, and interaction cadence.

You should have these inputs: (1) contact list, (2) roles, (3) interaction cadence. If any input is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Privacy rule: business role information only; no personal phone numbers or home emails, no performance or personality judgments about colleagues, and prefer role labels over named individuals where the role suffices. If the supplied contact list contains personal phone numbers or home emails, omit them from the output.

Method:
1. Read the contact list, roles, and interaction cadence provided below.
2. For each contact, produce a row: name, role, how they connect to me (e.g. "reviews my label claims," "owns formula changes," "external co-packer contact"), cadence (how often we interact), and channel (email, meetings, Teams, etc.).
3. Group contacts by function if a natural grouping emerges (e.g. internal regulatory/legal, R&D/formulation, marketing, external co-packer/supplier).
4. Do not invent a contact, role, or cadence not present in the inputs.
5. End with an install footer: state this map is best suited to Copilot Memory (for a small number of key contacts) or a private declarative agent's knowledge (for a larger, structured map). Memory entries are seeded by telling Copilot "Remember that <fact>" in chat, one contact fact per message, then verified and pruned in the Personalization pane (the pane itself is view and delete only; verify against your own tenant, since menus and rollout vary). A private declarative agent is built via Agent Builder at m365.cloud.microsoft/chat; sharing the agent beyond the specialist is admin-gated, and anything installed into an agent is visible to every future share recipient, so keep this contact map out of any agent that might be shared. Include a one-line verification step: ask Copilot who a specific contact is and confirm it reflects the installed map.

Source of truth: the contact list, roles, and interaction cadence provided below are the only sources.

This is durable context for the specialist to review and install themselves.

Do not fabricate a contact, connection, or cadence not present in the inputs.

name: team-roles-and-responsibilities
description: Records team roles, ownership, and escalation paths as durable context for a private declarative agent's instructions or knowledge.
when_to_use: Once, when setting up durable team context, and again after a team or ownership change.
what_to_use_for: Turning a team roster and ownership information into a structured roles-and-responsibilities record with RACI-style ownership and escalation paths.
required_inputs: Team roster; Ownership (who owns what, at least at a summary level)
expected_outputs: Roles plus RACI-style ownership (responsible, accountable, consulted, informed, per function); Escalation paths; Install footer naming the owning Copilot layer and load steps
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: record team roles, ownership, and escalation paths from a team roster and ownership information.

You should have these inputs: (1) team roster, (2) ownership information. If any input is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Privacy rule: business role information only; no personal phone numbers or home emails, no performance or personality judgments about colleagues (record who holds a role and its documented escalation route, never an assessment of anyone's capability), and prefer role labels over named individuals where the role suffices.

Method:
1. Read the team roster and ownership information provided below.
2. For each function relevant to labeling (formulation, regulatory/legal, marketing, QA, prepress/print, market surveillance), identify who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed, per the RACI model, using only roles present in the roster.
3. Build an escalation path for each function: who to escalate to first, and who is the final decision-maker, using only relationships stated or clearly implied by the roster and ownership data.
4. Do not invent a role, an ownership assignment, or an escalation path not supported by the inputs; mark a function as "owner not specified" if the roster does not name one.
5. End with an install footer: state this record is best suited to a private declarative agent's instructions or knowledge, built via Agent Builder at m365.cloud.microsoft/chat (Configure tab for instructions, or attached documents/sites for knowledge; verify against your own tenant, since menus and rollout vary), and note that pointing the agent at SharePoint/Graph content is metered and off by default, so a plain-text instructions version is the lower-friction starting point. Warn that anything installed into an agent is visible to every future share recipient, so this record belongs only in an agent that will stay private; note the saved markdown record is the durable source and the agent is a replaceable rendering of it. Include a one-line verification step: ask the agent who owns a specific function and confirm it matches this record.

Source of truth: the team roster and ownership information provided below are the only sources.

This is durable context for the specialist to review and install themselves.

Do not fabricate a role, an ownership assignment, or an escalation path not present in the inputs.

name: workstream-inventory
description: Inventories what the specialist is currently working on, as durable context for a private declarative agent's knowledge or Copilot Memory.
when_to_use: On a stated cadence: monthly, or alongside the weekly status report, whichever comes first, and additionally whenever workstreams change enough that Copilot's context on "what am I working on" would be stale.
what_to_use_for: Turning a list of current projects and workstreams into structured records with goal, status, stakeholders, and key artifacts, kept current as durable Copilot context.
expected_outputs: Workstream records (name, goal, status, stakeholders, artifacts, confidentiality flag); Review-by date for the whole inventory; Install footer naming the owning Copilot layer, load steps, and the remove-the-prior-version step
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: inventory the specialist's current workstreams from a list of current projects and workstreams.

You should have this input: (1) the list of current projects and workstreams. If it is missing or unreadable, stop and say so. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Privacy rule: business role information only; no personal phone numbers or home emails, no performance or personality judgments about colleagues, and prefer role labels over named individuals where the role suffices.

Confidentiality rule: unreleased SKU names, claims strategy, and launch timing stay out of any shareable layer; flag each workstream containing them as confidential so the specialist installs it only into a private, never-shared layer.

Method:
1. Read the current projects and workstreams provided below.
2. For each one, produce a record: name, goal (what it is trying to accomplish), status (using this project's status vocabulary: NEW, DRAFT, INPRG, REVIEW, DONE, ARCHIVED, plus a blocked flag if applicable), stakeholders (who else is involved), key artifacts (documents, SKUs, or files tied to it), and a confidential flag per the confidentiality rule.
3. Do not invent a workstream, a status, or a stakeholder not present in the inputs; if status is unclear from the input, mark it "unspecified" rather than guessing.
4. Add a review-by date for the whole inventory: one month from today, or the next weekly status report if sooner.
5. End with an install footer: state this inventory is best suited to a private declarative agent's knowledge (for a fuller record with attached documents) or Copilot Memory (for a short list of currently-active items), and note the tradeoff, a declarative agent needs Agent Builder setup at m365.cloud.microsoft/chat, while Memory is lower-friction but has less structure. Memory entries are seeded by telling Copilot "Remember that <fact>" in chat, one item per message, then verified and pruned in the Personalization pane (the pane itself is view and delete only; verify against your own tenant, since menus and rollout vary). State the remove-prior-version step: before installing, delete the superseded inventory's Memory entries in the Personalization pane or replace the agent's knowledge file, so stale context never persists. Include a one-line verification step: ask Copilot what you are currently working on and confirm the answer matches this inventory.

Source of truth: the current projects and workstreams provided below are the only sources.

This is durable context for the specialist to review and install themselves, and it must be refreshed by the review-by date since workstreams change.

Do not fabricate a workstream, a status, or a stakeholder not present in the inputs.
